title: Exact free module resolution of the augmentation on a total simplicial site
statement:
Let $\mathcal C_p$ ($p\ge0$) and $\mathcal D$ be small sites in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. For each order-preserving map $\alpha:[p]\to[q]$ in the simplex category [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object], let $u_\alpha:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_q)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_p)$ be a geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. Suppose their identity and composition identifications satisfy the cocycle laws, and let $a_p:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_p)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ have compatible coherent identifications $a_pu_\alpha\simeq a_q$. A total module is a family $F_p$ with transition maps $u_\alpha^{-1}F_p\to F_q$ compatible with these identifications. Fix a commutative ring $\Lambda$, use modules over its constant ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and use the canonical constant-coefficient inverse images. For a $\Lambda_{\mathcal D}$-module $G$, let $a^{-1}G$ be the total module with components $a_m^{-1}G$ and the augmentation identifications as transitions. Define $P_p(G)$ by
$$P_p(G)_m=\bigoplus_{\alpha:[p]\to[m]}a_m^{-1}G.$$
Its transition for $\beta:[m]\to[k]$ sends the $\alpha$ summand to the $\beta\alpha$ summand through $u_\beta^{-1}a_m^{-1}G\cong a_k^{-1}G$. For $p\ge1$ let $d_i:P_p(G)\to P_{p-1}(G)$ send the $\alpha$ summand in component $m$ identically to the $\alpha\delta_i$ summand, where $\delta_i:[p-1]\to[p]$ omits $i$. Let $\epsilon:P_0(G)\to a^{-1}G$ be the fold map in every component. These are morphisms of total modules, and the augmented chain complex with boundary $\sum_{i=0}^p(-1)^id_i$,
$$\cdots\longrightarrow P_2(G)\longrightarrow P_1(G)\longrightarrow P_0(G)\xrightarrow{\epsilon}a^{-1}G\longrightarrow0,$$
is exact. For every total module $I$, restriction of a morphism $P_p(G)\to I$ to the identity-labelled summand in component $p$ is a natural bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Tot}}(P_p(G),I)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{\Lambda_{\mathcal C_p}}(a_p^{-1}G,I_p).$$
Its inverse sends $f:a_p^{-1}G\to I_p$ on the $\alpha$ summand of component $m$ to $I(\alpha)\circ u_\alpha^{-1}f$, using $a_m^{-1}G\cong u_\alpha^{-1}a_p^{-1}G$. In particular $\epsilon$ corresponds to the identity when $I=a^{-1}G$.

proof.text: The canonical constant-coefficient inverse images preserve the cocycle identifications. On each summand, the transition along $\bigopluseta:[m]\to[k]$ is the specified comparison $u_\bigopluseta^{-1}a_m^{-1}G\cong a_k^{-1}G$ followed by relabelling $\alpha$ as $\bigopluseta\alpha$. The identity and composition cocycle laws make these transitions functorial, so they define total-module structures on $a^{-1}G$ and every $P_p(G)$. The same cocycle calculation shows each $d_i$ and the fold $\epsilon$ commute with transitions.

source.place: Tags 0D72 and 0D7C: ringed component construction and the direct-sum transition formula.

proof.text: Fix $m$. The component of the augmented complex is the tensor of $a_m^{-1}G$ with the augmented complex whose degree-$p$ term is the direct sum over all monotone maps $[p]\to[m]$, whose differential is the alternating face sum, and whose augmentation folds the degree-zero summands. By [lem-trf-total-site-simplex-free-resolution] this component complex is exact. By [lem-trf-total-site-component-restriction], total modules have componentwise kernels and images (the inverse-image functors are exact, as also supplied by [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image]). Therefore exactness at every component implies exactness in the category of total modules.

source.place: Tag 0D7C, proof after restriction to a component, identifying the complex with a constant module tensored with the simplex resolution.

proof.text: For a total module $I$, the universal property of the direct sum gives a morphism $P_p(G)\to I$ exactly when one specifies maps from each $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$ summand. Total compatibility forces every such component map to be $I(\alpha)\circ u_\alpha^{-1}f$, where $f$ is the map on the identity summand in component $p$; conversely these formulas satisfy the transition equations by the cocycle law. Thus restriction to the identity-labelled summand and the displayed extension formula are mutually inverse and natural.

source.place: Tag 0D72, direct-sum formula for $g_{n!}$ and its adjunction.

proof.text: The simplicial identities $\delta_i\delta_j=\delta_{j-1}\delta_i$ for $i<j$ imply cancellation of the two occurrences of every composite in the alternating sum, so the boundary squares to zero. The fold augmentation is compatible with transitions and is the identity on each degree-zero summand; under the identity-summand restriction bijection it corresponds to $1_{a^{-1}G}$ when $I=a^{-1}G$.

source.place: Tag 0D7C, specified face maps and augmentation; Tag 0D72, identity adjunction.

proof.text: All constructions use only the fixed coherent comparison maps and direct-sum inclusions, hence are natural in $G$ and in morphisms of total modules $I$. The componentwise exactness and the identity-summand bijection therefore hold simultaneously for the entire augmented complex, proving every assertion.
